It is shown that the ability to deal with co-channel interference is improved considerably. This is substantiated by a statistical assessment of the interference.

articleTitle: UPT and annoying interactions: How to deal with them?
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: In the next century, the concept of personal communication will assume more and more interest and importance. In fact, in order to meet the needs of the people on the move, the advanced personal communication capabilities will have to be offered "anywhere, at any time", making use of the essential functions provided by the Intelligent Network, e.g. for the registration, routing, charging and billing purposes, and also for its role of "core network" to provide the Universal Personal Telecommunication. It should be considered, anyway, that UPT will interact necessarily with other basic or supplementary services available in the network where the service is invoked; furthermore, the need of personal communications could conflict with third party rights. The interaction problem is also analysed in various environments, both within standardization bodies dealing with UPT or IN (e.g. in ETSI-NA7) and European research projects on IN matters (e.g. EURESCOM-P230). The aim of this paper is to present some examples of conflicting scenarios related to the above mentioned interactions, suggesting possible solutions to these problems.

articleTitle: Ants routing: An adaptive packet flow control scheme in multimedia communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: This paper reports on the advantages of introducing a novel adaptive congestion control algorithm on physical networks for multimedia communication at virtual channels and virtual paths' levels. The adaptive control begins when congestion appears on the network. The control strategy is based on the information of congestion that is monitored and revised according to congestion status at any time. Basically the network is composed of physical communication links and control lines between nodes in the network topology. Nodes are composed of a switching system for multimedia users, a protocol converter, a knowledge-based flow control system for the multimedia network, a router, and a network interface. From/to the network node, actual information is exchanged and knowledge-based information for flow control is also exchanged. As a result, one can obtain the prospective trends in intelligent flow control to avoid the congestion of multimedia information on the network.

articleTitle: Development of PCS in Directorate General of Telecommunications, Taiwan R.O.C
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: Personal Communication Services (PCS) is a set of capabilities that allows some combination of terminal mobility, personal mobility and service profile management. In other words, PCS allows a person, by employing a unique personal number, to access telecommunications services anytime, anywhere, and with the services controllable by the person himself or herself. PCS has been widely recognized as one of the most significant growth areas in telecommunications for the decade to come. This paper summarizes the PCS development plan in Directorate General of Telecommunications (DGT) in Taiwan, Republic of China. Also, the PCS R&D activities in Telecommunication Laboratories, a research institute under DGT, are described in more detail, including intelligent network for PCS, wireless access technology, propagation measurement and modeling, and RF technology.

articleTitle: Simulation study of central frequency offset for time spread and despread filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The authors have simulated the time spread and despread filters as digital filters. Basically they work well and the possibility of constructing a CDMA network with these kinds of filters is shown. The central frequency offset problem is also discussed and it is found that it is necessary to limit the frequency offset quantity within 1/4 of a chip bandwidth in order to prevent the processing gain degradation less than 3dB. The intersymbol interference due to the ripples of the despread signals is also a problem which needs further study.

articleTitle: Characterization of wireless indoor communication channel: Measurements and simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The growing interest in wireless indoor transmission systems and practical applications of local area networks have resulted in many investigations on the propagation of radio waves inside buildings. Most of the work done in this field aims at experimentally obtaining the statistical characteristics of the signal. The results presented in this paper give a better understanding of the propagation behavior of 37.2 GHz signals in different environments, making it possible to predict the time delay propagation from a knowledge of the building structure. Reflections from walls also play a major role in maintaining a high signal level within a closed environment. These results encourage the application of this type of radio system for the development of secure local communication systems in well defined environments. In fact, most common building materials used for external walls and room partitioning are very effective in screening the signal. From the foregoing results, a highly unified numerical procedure to treat the complex bounded electromagnetic field problems is needed. Furthermore, a solution of the 3-D mathematical model based on the time-domain integral equation of the electric field is proposed using the Boundary Element Method.

articleTitle: Virtual angle diversity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The paper takes advantage of the motion of a vehicle in an urban mobile radio environment to create a virtual antenna array out of a single antenna. Based on root-MUSIC, the virtual array is used to resolve up to two Doppler frequencies. In an IS-54 environment, the resolved frequencies correspond to the two clusters of incoming radio waves (specified by TR45.3.2) assuming that each cluster has a unique Doppler frequency. Once the Doppler frequencies are resolved, notch filtering is used to separate the two clusters hence forcing the channel to be frequency-flat. Once the two clusters have been separated, they can be combined as a second order angle diversity system.

articleTitle: Delay and throughput characteristics of TH, CDMA, TDMA, and hybrids for multipath faded data transmission channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: This work introduces the new concepts of adaptive time hopping and variable frame Code Division (CDMA) Multiple Access, and evaluates by a unified analysis the probabilities of bit and packet errors in multipath fading environment of five Time Division (TDMA), Code Division, and Time Hopping (TH) related multiaccess networks, namely: TDMA, CDMA, CDMA/TDMA, Adaptive CDMA/TH, and variable frame CDMA/TDMA networks. The delay and useful throughputs of the five systems are also evaluated for data and voice traffics. All systems use the same channel power and bandwidth, and support the same traffic. Though implementation issues are not covered, CDMA systems are put at a disadvantage by ignoring such inherent advantages as voice silence utilizations and automatic frequency reuse (compared to cellular-type FDMA networks for example). Not surprisingly, CDMA systems 4 and 5 outperform TDMA systems at low and medium input traffics.

articleTitle: Solar power supplied multi-purposes radio information system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: Local area community broadcast provides various kinds of information for behaving persons and residents in the district. According to an experience of 70MHz band community broadcast at Hakodate City in Hokkaido, transmission power is about 0.5W and its servicing area is more than 5 km of radius. The first author has developed computer software and a simple operating method for weather forecast by using a set of local weather conditions observed at hourly intervals. The solar battery makes he energy self support systems possible at secluded places among the mountains, national parks and solitary islands that required no power plants, no wire and poles, no exhausts and clean natural environments.

articleTitle: An asynchronous digital demodulator for TDMA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: BNR Europe Limited has developed a digitally realised demodulator for use in Time Division Multiple Access mobile communication systems. This is aimed particularly at low power, low cost in-building wireless, specifically the DECT system, and is compatible with other common angle modulation standards. The demodulator includes sampling at IF, digital down conversion and phase discrimination followed by digital timing recovery and burst correlation. The demodulator deals with the problem of variable burst to burst timing requiring fast capture of the optimum bit timing position with a minimum overhead. This is achieved by novel symbol timing estimation using an asynchronous system clock avoiding the need for storage of the entire burst. The paper describes the principles of the design together with aspects of its practical implementation as relevant. The paper concludes with a discussion of the measured performance.

articleTitle: The role of cordless communications in PCS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: PCS is often identified with mobile/cellular systems, e.g. DCS1800 (sometimes referred to as PCN, it is a standard for GSM on 1800 MHz). Personal Communications Systems aiming for a broad subscriber basis must however comprise many systems (existing and future). As cordless system provides very high capacity (DECT /spl ap/ 10,000 Erlang/km//sup 2/floor), they are likely to be considerable part of PCS. Advanced cordless systems as DECT (Digital European Cordless Telecommunications) are easy to adapt to and integrate with other systems as ISDN, GSM, PSTN etc. This paper describes the main features and applications of DECT and the concept of "profiles" in DECT facilitating a deep integration with other systems.

articleTitle: The networking of dynamic satellite constellations in a global personal communication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: Networking issues relating to Personal Mobile Satellite Communication Systems are discussed in this paper. These issues are of direct relevance to the various Dynamic Satellite Constellations (DSCs) which have been proposed for such applications. A baseline DSC Network architecture is initially introduced and explained. Alternative Networking approaches to User Mobility Management and Network Resource Management are then described. Signalling overheads and protocol delay are the important parameters considered.

articleTitle: A novel approach to frequency synthesis and modulation using quadratic correlation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: Due to the severe FM-TDMA constraints imposed in the established and emerging Personal Communication Systems, it is necessary to perform fast frequency channel switching. This feature, together with the modulation characteristic, that requires a bandwidth close to the interchannel switching ratio, make it difficult to merge both modulation and channelization in the same single loop structure. In fact, a PLL synthesizer damping factor has to be so low that it destroys the modulation if no special care is taken. The present paper shows some architecture and analytical studies, in order to obtain joined modulation and channelization, with a single loop synthesizer using a quadratic correlation loop.

articleTitle: Spectrum management methodology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: In many countries, spectrum will be cleared before reallocation to PCS, however, in some countries (e.g. U.S.A.), clear spectrum will not initially be available for licensed PCS operators and some flexible management scheme will be needed to use all allocated spectrum, which is available at a specific location. In all countries, flexible spectrum allocation is desirable due to changes over time, between applications and between operators. Spectrum Management Methodology (SMM), discussed in this paper, is a flexible technology for dynamically handling local optimization of spectrum resources in licensed bands and supports the use of non-contiguous blocks of spectrum. SMM can be used to flexibly control the use of spectrum to reflect different application requirements, regulatory changes in allocation, local spectrum availability and local operator mix. SMM is currently envisioned for deployment in the U.S. Emerging Technologies band, but could be developed to support future applications (e.g. FPLMTS) or other countries, where different spectrum may be allocated.

articleTitle: An efficient adaptive structure for interference rejection and PN correlation simultaneously in DS spread-spectrum system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The author propose an efficient interference rejection filter structure for direct-sequence spread-spectrum systems. Unlike the existing structures, the proposed adaptive filter performs interference rejection and pseudorandom sequence correlation simultaneously. The number of arithmetic operations required to implement the structure is reduced significantly as compared to existing algorithms. Compared with the performance of the system proposed by Li and Milstein (1982) the proposed system yields improved mean-square error (MSE), especially in the high range of the signal-to-Gaussian noise ratio.

articleTitle: UPT implementation in a CS1 network environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: While personal communications services are being implemented in various ways, there are advantages in migrating to a common environment. This paper considers how the CCITT Universal Personal Telecommunication (UPT) service may be implemented within the CCITT Intelligent Network Capability Set 1 (CS1) environment. There will be strong incentives to do this form from a standardization, feature evolution, and network interworking point of view, once CS1 is available and UPT is fully defined. The basic characteristics of UPT and CS1 are reviewed, and a number of key implementation aspects are examined. The manner in which UPT may be implemented using the service independent building blocks provided by CS1 is illustrated, and the extent to which CS1 supports the currently defined UPT features is identified. Options and issues associated with the overall network structure are discussed, and an appropriate UPT network architecture is proposed. Also discussed is the evolution from a near-term non-CS1 environment to the longer-term full CS1 environment.

articleTitle: A service logic program structure of UPT service in intelligent networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: A single SLP may be a solution for UPT services. However, the authors propose a strategy of building UPT services with multiple SLPs which can be triggered independently. They also discuss a structure that treats these SLPs as a single SLP. These structures make it easy to enhance UPT services, because additional SLPs may introduce new UPT features independently. Furthermore, the relationship is clarified between personal mobility and UPT service's SLP triggering, the cooperation of adjacent UPT service SLPs, and the required functions to support SLP cooperation.

articleTitle: Performance study of two optimal detectors of asynchronous CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: To date, most available CDMA systems are interference limited. Although many schemes have been proposed to reduce the effects of interferences, few of them are based on optimal criteria. The maximum likelihood sequence detector (MLSD) is one of the few detectors that is optimal. However, it has a complexity growing exponentially with the number of users, and is not implementable for many practical applications. This paper shows that, as long as the number of users in the system is kept moderate, the performance of the MLSD can be approached by a simple linear detector that is based on an optimal estimator.

articleTitle: Grade of service simulator for GSM radio cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: BNR Europe Limited has developed a Monte-Carlo Simulator for networks of GSM radio cells. The simulator outputs Grade of Service measurements such as: probability of call blocking, probability of call failure, averaged C/I measurements for the region simulated and numbers of handovers generated in the system. The purpose of the Simulator is to examine the effect of operating parameters in the GSM system upon the system performance and to evaluate algorithms for the control of GSM systems. This paper describes the Simulator and illustrates its use, for instance, in showing that handover performance is very sensitive to the parameter HO-MARGIN.

articleTitle: Selection process of Canadian telecommunications service providers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The Canadian Department of Communications uses a comparative selection process for radio frequency spectrum assignment and licensing. The process is used when foreseen immediate demand exceeds the availability of spectrum, this often occurs with the introduction of new telecommunications services. It is effective in meeting the Department's spectrum management responsibilities of radio frequency assignment, radio station license issuance and responding to the demands of the public. The public land-mobile telecommunications services that were introduced utilizing the process are: cellular mobile radiotelephone (1983), 400 MHz and 800 MHz mobile radio trunked systems (1983), 900 MHz nation-wide paging (1989 and 1991), air-ground radiotelephone (1992), and public digital cordless telephone (1992). This paper reviews the Canadian legislative context in which the process operates, the current comparative selection process, and factors that influence the process.

articleTitle: EHF planar array measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: A 30 cm /spl times/ 37 cm dual-band (Tx: 28.4 GHz, Rx: 19.2 GHz) microstrip planar antenna has been developed for a suitcase satellite Personal Communications terminal. Antenna measurements have been performed in the laboratory, in a far-field range, rooftop range, over the Olympus satellite (gain) and in a spherical near-field range (complete characterization). The design goal for the antenna was to achieve a minimum Tx gain of 34.7 dBi and Rx gain of 33.3 dBi over 1 GHz of bandwidth. The problems encountered in measuring this relatively large antenna (30 /spl lambda/) and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Improved coded transceivers for personal and mobile communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: In this work, the performance of trellis coded modulation with improved non-coherent receivers is examined for application to personal and mobile satellite communications. The schemes are analyzed and evaluated in additive white Gaussian noise, Rayleigh, Rician and shadowed channels. Evaluations have shown that the improved non-coherent receivers are capable of providing considerable improvement in performance as compared to the conventional differential receivers.

articleTitle: CT2 Plus Class2:A potential for quality transmission performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The CT2Plus Class 2 audio requirements specification produced under the auspices of the Radio Advisory Board of Canada (RABC) provides guidance to manufacturers on how to build quality product. The focus of this contribution is to discuss the performance of these terminals in the context of an error free radio environment. It is concluded that terminals which met these voluntary RABC standards have the potential of providing quality transmission performance when operated in an error free radio environment.

articleTitle: Network aspects relevant to the integration between the GSM network and a satellite system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The integration between cellular and satellite systems permits to provide wider and more efficient area coverage. In this paper the viability of a full integration between the GSM cellular network and a spot-beam satellite system is dealt with. The integration analysis focuses on the network aspects. Full integration means to reuse, as far as possible, the same equipment and protocols, i.e. the same hardware and software, for the satellite and the GSM network. In the integrated system the user need not be aware whether the actual connection goes through the satellite or the GSM network. The paper identifies the most promising satellite system configuration and the satellite system counterpart of the GSM functional areas (cell, location area, MSC area). Moreover, the problems and the relevant solutions related to the extension of the GSM procedures (e.g. call set-up, cell selection/reselection, handover, initial acquisition, tracking) to the satellite system are dealt with.

articleTitle: An experimental slow frequency-hopped personal communication system for the proposed U.S. 1850-1990 MHz band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: An operational, prototype 1.8 GHz personal communication system employing the access technique of slow frequency-hopped CDMA is described. This system was designed to permit true vehicular/portable mobility with larger cells than conventional PCS proposals would allow while providing for the existence of a lower-cost PCS which would be operable in truly pedestrian-only environments. In the paper, the modem architecture, algorithms, and performance are discussed. The system has been found to yield excellent performance on a variety of channels characteristic of expanded PCS environment at a reasonable level of hardware complexity.

articleTitle: Design considerations for a broadband indoor wireless system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The growth of wireless personal communications systems (PCS) in the coming decade is expected to be dramatic, with some projected forecasts for the U.S. market alone of the order of $3 billion by 1997. At the same time, the full-scale development of high-speed ATM-switched networks and the evolution towards 'third generation' portables will make the integration of wireless and optical systems not only desirable but necessary. This study considers a future indoor wireless network operating in the MM-wavelength spectrum and capable of supporting broadband services like video teleconferencing and transmission of high resolution images on top of the traditional ones that include cordless telephony and paging. A point of view and a general framework for the interface of this system to a public switched ATM network are suggested here.

articleTitle: A suitable architecture for personal communications systems based on small satellites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The strategic importance of developing a world-wide personal communication service through user's hand-held terminals has been carried out by the space-industry. Therefore, next step of this process is the assessment of all system implementation aspects. This paper deals with a satellite system, based on a Low Earth Orbit constellation, offering an optimum system architecture based on small simple (transparent or purely regenerative) satellites. All major critical aspects relevant to the space segment and to the ground segment are examined. In particular, the orbital constellation parameters are discussed in order to minimise, with the assumed traffic distribution, the number of satellites and to offer high availability in terms of number of circuits and service time-continuity. Different hypotheses for the payload architecture are proposed: depending on the access method selected (CDMA, TDMA, and mixed are discussed), and taking into account the low complexity space-segment requirements to achieve the low cost goal for the overall system. A preliminary dimensioning of the derived spacecraft options is also presented. Finally, this paper addresses the major networking aspects, focusing on the impact and the integrability of the proposed satellite system with the existing or planned terrestrial infrastructure for Personal Communications. In particular, the main network requirements, in terms of functionalities, topology and architecture are pointed out.

articleTitle: Security architecture in the UMTS network - A comparison with the FPLMTS network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: Second generation mobile networks, as the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) and the Digital European Cordless Telecommunications (DECT) have been studied in the environment of the European mobile communications. These networks will be used for the nineties. However, third generation mobile communications are being developed in order to join these networks and to provide a single access. This paper claims to give a description of the Universal Mobile Telecommunication System (UMTS) and the Future Public Land Mobile Telecommunications Systems (FPLMTS) and to make a comparison between them with regard to security. For this purpose, several aspects of security mainly related to function entities, security architecture, call handling and location management are specially studied for both systems. The UMTS network is being developed within the European Commission's Research on Advanced Communications in Europe (RACE) in order to give telephonic mobile support in Europe and the rest of the world in the 2000s. In the UMTS network planning, an interface with other networks like the Universal Personal Telecommunications (UPT) has been defined and its integration with Broadband Integrated Services Digital Networks (BISDN) is being studied. Likewise it would be advisable to establish the compatibility between UMTS and FPLMTS.

articleTitle: A pilot based dynamic channel assignment scheme for wireless access TDMA/FDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The authors propose control architecture for implementing a dynamic channel assignment (DCA) algorithm which optimizes two-way channel quality in a TDMA portable radio system. A common control frequency, which is frame-synchronized among base stations, provides (1) beacons for portables to locate base-stations and obtain DCA information, (2) broadcast channels for system and alerting information, and (3) pilot signals to permit portables to evaluate downlink interference. This allows low-complexity radio ports and portables to simultaneously select channels to avoid interference and avoid creating excessive interference. Only local measurements are needed for this autonomous DCA scheme, thus avoiding processing by a centralized controller or communications among distributed controllers. A superframe structure on the control frequency provides redundant information for the beacon and pilot signals to avoid the "blind-slot" problems which cause significant difficulty in other systems for the link transfer (hand off) process. Results from computer simulations demonstrate the good spectrum efficiency of this method. They also show that power control further improves the performance significantly. This work is targeted towards understanding the implications to local exchange networks of wireless system alternatives that could provide access to those networks.

articleTitle: RFICs for reduced size, cost and power consumption in handheld wireless transceivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The high volume potential of existing and proposed wireless Personal Communications Systems in the 800-2500 MHz frequency range presents tremendous challenges and opportunities to designers and suppliers of RFICs. Amplifiers, oscillators, frequency converters and synthesizers are now required to operate from lower supply voltages, consume less current and reduce their physical size while meeting aggressive targets for performance, quality, cost and uniformity. This paper describes Silicon Bipolar and GaAs RFIC process technologies which are particularly well suited to this market. Furthermore, the roles of existing and future RFICs, hybrid modules and discrete devices for a typical RF system architecture in a half-duplex digital radio are discussed. Some key technical constraints that impact the performance of RFIC components at supply voltages of 3V or less are also illustrated in detail.

articleTitle: Adaptation of land mobile systems for onboard operation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: The operation of Personal Communication Systems' (PCS) during air travel time, has already been recognized as a formal user requirement. However, the existing and planned onboard communication systems for public services, the Aeronautical Passenger Communications (APC), have not been originally designed to support onboard operation of PCS. Further, a number of functional restrictions are imposed when such systems get airborne. In this paper, the authors discuss potential solution(s) for extending PCS mobility into the demanding environment of air travelling. The possibilities offered by the Aeronautical Telecommunication Network architecture are investigated, and practical alternatives are proposed. In addition, adaptation of existing PCSs, as well as extra requirements for the coming 3rd generation ones, for achieving interoperability with avionics subnetworks, are examined.

articleTitle: Bell Atlantic PCS market trial Testing activities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2nd IEEE International Conference on Universal Personal Communications
abstract: This paper describes a rigorous and extensive testing program that was designed and executed for the Personal Line Trial. This program covered various technical areas, as well as service issues. The testing covered many network elements/systems in many different configurations. Due to the cooperation of Bell Atlantic, BAMS, Bell of Pennsylvania, Bellcore, and all the suppliers participating in the testing program, many early discrepancies were identified and corrected in time for the Personal Line trial. This testing program provided not only some confidence that the service is technically robust and acceptable to end users, but also some assurance that introducing this new service would not adversely affect the normal operation of the network.
